sources.title: AG James Secures Court Order Against Donald J. Trump, Trump Children, And Trump Foundation
Judge Says Trump Must Pay $2 Million Over Misuse Of Foundation Funds

supported_event_claim: On November 7, 2019, a New York judge ordered Donald Trump to pay $2 million in damages for improperly using Trump Foundation charitable funds to further his 2016 presidential campaign and his personal interests, with Trump admitting to misusing funds.
reason: The New York Attorney General's official press release confirms the court order, Trump's admissions, and the $2 million penalty on November 7, 2019; NPR independently reported the same judgment.

sources.title: Trump makes unscheduled visit to Walter Reed hospital

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump made an unscheduled visit to Walter Reed National Military Medical Center on November 16-17, 2019, which the White House described as the start of a physical exam.
reason: AP confirmed the unscheduled Walter Reed visit. Subsequent reporting from September 2020 revealed Trump had mischaracterized the visit when denying a mini-stroke allegation from Michael Schmidt's book.

sources.title: New book claims Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell worked for Mossad

supported_event_claim: A book titled 'Epstein: Dead Men Tell No Tales,' published in December 2019, included claims by former Israeli intelligence officer Ari Ben-Menashe that Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell worked for Israeli intelligence.
reason: The NY Post reported on the book's publication and Ben-Menashe's claims about Epstein and Maxwell's alleged intelligence ties, which is the primary claim documented in this entry.

sources.title: Giuliani Returns From Ukraine Trip and Signals He Will Brief Trump

supported_event_claim: Rudy Giuliani traveled to Ukraine in late November/early December 2019, where he met with pro-Russia Ukrainian official and parliament member Andriy Derkach; One America News filmed the meeting.
reason: NYT reported on Giuliani's Ukraine trip and his meeting with Derkach, who was later sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury for interfering in the 2020 election as a Russian agent.

sources.title: Private Conservative Group Laid Plans to Contest 2020 Election Results Months Before Votes Were Cast

supported_event_claim: Members of ALEC and the Council for National Policy met as part of a 'Political Process Working Group' in December 2019 at the States and Nation Policy Summit, discussing strategies for challenging election results.
reason: ProPublica's investigation documented the ALEC/CNP Political Process Working Group meetings, including the December 2019 SNPS session, and the group's early planning to contest election results.

supported_event_claim: No credible independently verifiable news source confirms that the FBI received a laptop and hard drive containing Hunter Biden files on or before December 9, 2019.
reason: The precise date the FBI acquired the laptop is disputed and the specific framing of this entry — including the claim the material was available for purchase in Ukraine for $5 million — is not corroborated by credible contemporaneous news reporting. The origin and chain of custody of the Hunter Biden laptop remain contested; no major outlet confirmed the December 9, 2019 FBI acquisition date as presented here.

sources.title: Louis DeJoy donated more than $600,000 to Trump and Republicans as he lobbied for USPS role

supported_event_claim: Louis DeJoy, then the RNC finance chairman, donated more than $600,000 to Donald Trump's campaign and the Republican National Committee between October 2019 and December 2019, overlapping with the period after the previous Postmaster General announced her resignation.
reason: WaPo's investigation documented DeJoy's large donations to Trump and Republican causes, and their timing relative to the USPS Postmaster General vacancy, raising conflict-of-interest concerns.

sources.title: Whistleblower: DHS told to alter assessments to match Trump's views

supported_event_claim: Acting Deputy DHS Secretary Ken Cuccinelli ordered DHS intelligence officials to alter or suppress intelligence assessments that conflicted with Donald Trump's political rhetoric, including ordering analysts fired or reassigned for not conforming their reports to Trump's messaging.
reason: AP reported on the DHS whistleblower complaint by Brian Murphy, which documented Cuccinelli's directive to fire or reassign analysts whose reports contradicted Trump's views; the December 2019 meeting is cited in that complaint.

sources.title: FBI told Sanders that Russia is working to help his campaign

supported_event_claim: The FBI briefed Bernie Sanders or his campaign that Russia was boosting him online in an effort to help him win the Democratic nomination and then face Trump in the general election, with intelligence assessing the Kremlin believed Sanders was Trump's best opponent.
reason: WaPo reported in February 2020 that the FBI briefed Sanders on Russian efforts to boost his candidacy, framing it as a means to help Trump win re-election.

sources.title: Trump attends Palm Beach police and fire ball at Mar-a-Lago

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump attended the Palm Beach Police and Fire Foundation's annual ball at Mar-a-Lago on January 19, 2020, giving a speech and interacting with guests.
reason: The Palm Beach Post, the local paper of record for the area, reported directly on Trump's appearance at the annual fundraising ball, which was a ticketed public event.

sources.title: Iran lawmaker announces $3 million reward for killing Trump

supported_event_claim: Iranian lawmaker Ahmad Hamzeh announced a $3 million bounty for the assassination of Donald Trump on January 21, 2020, as retaliation for the U.S. drone strike that killed General Qasem Soleimani.
reason: Reuters reported on Hamzeh's bounty announcement, confirming it was an individual lawmaker's offer without indication of Iranian government backing.

sources.title: Russian Court Orders Removal of FBI and Interpol Information About Semion Mogilevich
sources.publisher: Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP)

supported_event_claim: A Russian court in Kislovodsk ruled on February 3, 2020 that online information about Semion Mogilevich, including FBI and Interpol records, must be removed from the internet.
reason: OCCRP reported on the Russian court ruling banning online distribution of information about Mogilevich, a key investigative organization covering organized crime and corruption in Russia.

sources.title: Inside the move to install a Trump ally as postmaster general

supported_event_claim: In early February 2020, Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin met with Republican USPS Board of Governors members to discuss finding a new Postmaster General who would support Donald Trump's agenda for the agency.
reason: WaPo's reporting on how DeJoy came to be Postmaster General documented Mnuchin's involvement in steering the selection process toward a Trump-aligned candidate, with the meeting occurring in early 2020.

sources.title: Read the full transcript of Trump's impeachment acquittal speech

supported_event_claim: On February 6, 2020, Donald Trump delivered an extended address at the White House in which he celebrated his Senate acquittal, attacked political opponents and the Russia investigation, and provided a wide-ranging personal statement on his presidency.
reason: Vox published the full transcript of Trump's post-acquittal speech, which is the direct documentation of the event described in the entry.

sources.title: Intelligence chiefs cancel annual worldwide threat hearing

supported_event_claim: U.S. intelligence community officials declined to appear before Congress for the annual Worldwide Threats hearings in February 2020, with sources indicating officials feared their testimony on issues like Russia would anger Trump following his acquittal.
reason: Politico reported on February 7, 2020 that intelligence leaders cancelled the annual hearings, citing sources who said officials feared presidential anger over topics including Russian election interference.

sources.title: Trump Admits Virus's Lethality to Woodward in February but Told Public It Was 'Under Control'

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump told journalist Bob Woodward on February 7, 2020 that COVID-19 was deadly and airborne, while publicly telling Americans the virus would disappear by April 2020 and was under control.
reason: NYT reporting on the Woodward book documented Trump's contradictory private and public statements about COVID-19 starting in February 2020, revealing the gap between what he knew and what he told the public.

sources.title: Senate Republican blocks two bills aimed at securing elections

supported_event_claim: Senator Marsha Blackburn blocked two bills on February 11-12, 2020 that would have banned internet-connected voting machines and required campaigns to report foreign offers of election assistance.
reason: The Hill reported on Blackburn's objections blocking the two election security bills from advancing in the Senate, with Blackburn accusing Democrats of partisan motives.

sources.title: Trump ousts intel chief Maguire, installs loyalist Grenell

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump replaced Acting Director of National Intelligence Joseph Maguire with Richard Grenell on February 20, 2020, following classified congressional testimony about Russia boosting Trump's 2020 campaign that angered the president.
reason: AP reported on Trump's decision to replace Maguire with Grenell, confirming the background of the congressional briefing about Russia interference that precipitated the move.

sources.title: Trump Names Loyalist With No Intelligence Experience as Acting Spy Chief

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump named Richard Grenell, a Fox News commentator and Trump loyalist with no intelligence experience, as Acting Director of National Intelligence on February 20, 2020, replacing Joseph Maguire.
reason: NYT contemporaneously reported on Grenell's appointment and his lack of intelligence community experience, raising concerns about politicization of U.S. intelligence.

sources.title: Trump campaign spokesperson Kayleigh McEnany: Trump will always protect American citizens; we will not see diseases like coronavirus come here

supported_event_claim: Trump campaign spokesperson Kayleigh McEnany told Fox News on February 25, 2020 that the coronavirus would not come to the United States because Trump would always protect American citizens.
reason: Media Matters documented and archived McEnany's Fox News statement dismissing the threat of coronavirus reaching the United States, made two weeks before the WHO declared a pandemic.

sources.title: Russia Secretly Offered Afghan Militants Bounties to Kill U.S. Troops, Intelligence Says

supported_event_claim: U.S. intelligence officials determined that Russia's GRU paid bounties to Taliban-linked militants to kill American troops in Afghanistan, and that Trump was briefed on this intelligence in early 2020 but took no action.
reason: NYT broke the story on June 26, 2020, reporting that Trump received intelligence about Russia's bounty program on U.S. troops in Afghanistan but neither retaliated nor formally acknowledged the program.

sources.title: Private Conservative Group Laid Plans to Contest 2020 Election Results Months Before Votes Were Cast

supported_event_claim: ALEC CEO Lisa Nelson told attendees at a Council for National Policy conference in late February 2020 that ALEC was working with Republican attorneys to find paths 'to question the validity of an election.'
reason: ProPublica documented this CNP conference session and Lisa Nelson's remarks about ALEC working on strategies to challenge election results, months before the 2020 general election.

sources.title: Donald Trump Jr. accuses Democrats of hoping the coronavirus 'comes here and kills millions of people'

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump Jr. appeared on Fox News on February 29, 2020 and accused Democrats of hoping the coronavirus would spread to the U.S. and kill millions of Americans to harm Trump's re-election chances.
reason: Business Insider reported on Trump Jr.'s Fox News appearance and his accusation that Democrats were hoping for a coronavirus outbreak for political gain.

sources.title: Remarks by President Trump at the Conservative Political Action Conference

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump delivered remarks at the 2020 Conservative Political Action Conference on February 29, 2020, covering topics including Russia, the Mueller investigation, and political opponents.
reason: The Trump White House archived the full transcript of the 2020 CPAC speech on the official White House website, which is now preserved at the National Archives version of trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov.

sources.title: Inside Peter Navarro's Months-Long Quest to Lock In Contracts for Covid-19 Supplies

supported_event_claim: White House trade adviser Peter Navarro warned Trump on March 1, 2020 that COVID-19 required urgent action, and over the following weeks directed large contracts for COVID supplies to companies ill-equipped to fulfill them.
reason: NYT reported on Navarro's unilateral pandemic procurement activity, including his March 1 memo to Trump urging rapid action, and his subsequent direction of over $1 billion in contracts to companies without drug manufacturing capacity.
